title: hotfix: tighten SLO enforcer backoff thresholds and regional failover ordering to prevent cascading load-shedding
author: Aisha Kapoor
description: Motivation: After the incident on 2026-02-27 we observed pathological interactions between the SLO enforcer backoff and the regional failover controller. Under partial regional congestion the enforcer would aggressively back off traffic from healthy regional pools too quickly, causing downstream capacity thrashing and increased global load-shedding. This hotfix tightens the enforcer backoff thresholds, adds a short stabilization window before escalating failover, and reorders regional failover evaluation so that local capacity is preferred for transient spikes. Summary of changes: 1) Reduce enforcer backoff multiplier (default from 2.0 -> 1.3) and cap maximum backoff to 30s. 2) Add stabilization window (configurable 10s) before triggering regional failover escalation. 3) Change failover evaluation order to prefer local healthy pools with KV-cache affinity heuristics. 4) Add metrics and traces for backoff decisions and failover reasons. 5) Add unit and integration tests that simulate partial-region congestion. Rollout plan: apply hotfix to staging, run perf-canary scenario (regional spike) for 30m, then canary to 10% of traffic in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 for 2h, monitor slo_enforcer.backoff.rate and slo_enforcer.failover.count; if regressions observed rollback to previous tag. Backward compatibility: config knobs are additive and default to previous behavior only at historical thresholds; operators can tune. Revert strategy: revert commit or set enforcer.backoff.multiplier to 2.0 via runtime config. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration canary test - [x] Metrics/alerts added - [x] Docs updated (runtime config reference) - [x] Post-deploy monitoring dashboard tile
